# Tower of Hanoi (3 blocks): Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `tower-of-hanoi.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.34) and `tower-of-hanoi-rules.soar` (11 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`). Needs Soar 9.6.6.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . tower-of-hanoi.soar --seed 1 --cap 300000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . tower-of-hanoi.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py tower-of-hanoi init-tower3.world

`gen.py` regenerates the rules (`tools/rosie_tasks.py`, function `hanoi`); `python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with
another example state as the initial world, for the state checks.

## Results (Soar 9.6.6, library v2.34, 16 Nov 2026)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`) | init-tower3: goal false; final-tower3: goal true |
| Seeds 1-3, library defaults | solved, 7 moves each (the shortest), 35,392 / 44,437 / 46,450 decisions; seed 1 takes 19 s |
| Independent replay (`check_plan.py`) | every move legal, goal holds |
| Settings probe (P6, `probe.json`) | operator depth: 21 moves over 3 seeds, 126,279 decisions; tie-impasse: 216 moves, 344,708 decisions. Library defaults kept |

## Assumption ledger (places where the English is open)

| ID | Reading |
|---|---|
| A-H1 | "clear" is defined for a location ("If a location is not below an object") but used for "a clear block". Read as: any object that is not below an object is clear. |
| A-H4 | "move X onto Y": X's on relation and the matching below relation now name Y; the object X left becomes clear. |
| A-H2 | "larger than" is defined with the block as subject and used with the object as subject. Read as: X is larger than Y when X's volume is more than Y's. |
| A-H3 | "two clear green locations": two different green locations, both clear (the world has exactly two). |
| A-H5 | The action has no name in the dialog; it is called `move`. |

Convention notes: `clear` is a maintained one-argument relation (W-SPEC v6 section 3); `larger than` is expanded in place; the goal is `^goal-met` on the task object.

The decision counts are high because nothing in the instructions limits the search: there is no rule against undoing the last move and no repeated-state avoidance, so the look-ahead searches move sequences depth by depth, up to depth 7, without pruning. Since 16 Nov (afternoon) the rules come from the shared `tools/rosie_tasks.py`; the generated agent behaves identically (seed 1: 7 moves, 35,393 decisions).
